sections.overview: The Little Curlew is the smallest curlew, breeding in northern Siberia and migrating to Australasia.
sections.identification: It has a short, gently curved bill and is far smaller than the Far Eastern Curlew (Numenius madagascariensis); the Whimbrel (N. phaeopus) is larger and bulkier.
sections.habitat: It nests in open clearings and river valleys in northern Siberia, then winters mainly in northern Australia on inland grasslands and wetlands.
sections.diet: It feeds by picking prey from the surface and probing only shallowly, often on short grass or wet ground.
sections.behavior: Away from the breeding grounds it often gathers in large flocks and makes long seasonal journeys between Siberia and Australasia.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground in the northern breeding range, sometimes in loose colonies, and generally lays four eggs.
sections.ecology: Unlike the coastal Far Eastern Curlew, the Little Curlew often uses inland grasslands and floodplains during the Australian wet season.
sections.conservation: BirdLife's 2024 global assessment lists it as Least Concern, although the population trend is reported as decreasing.
